claim: Groeningemuseum holds Flemish Primitives masterworks by Jan van Eyck, Hans Memling, Hugo van der Goes and Gerard David from late 15th-early 16th-century Bruges.
quote: The Groeninge Museum provides a varied overview of the history of Belgian visual art, with top-class paintings by the world-renowned Flemish primitives.

claim: Sint-Janshospitaal houses four of Hans Memling's seven masterpieces in a preserved medieval hospital; Musea Brugge holds the world's second-largest Memling collection.
quote: Musea Brugge's Memling collection is the second largest in the world.

claim: Memling's Shrine of St Ursula (c.1489), a carved gilded reliquary with oil-on-panel inserts (87x33x91 cm), is on display in the Old St John's Hospital, Bruges.
quote: The Shrine of St. Ursula is a carved and gilded wooden reliquary containing oil on panel inserts (87x33x91 cm) by Hans Memling, dating to c. 1489, and is housed in the Hans Memling Museum in the Old St. John's Hospital.

claim: The Gruuthuse, a late-Gothic 15th-century city palace expanded by Lodewijk van Gruuthuse, takes its name from the gruit herb-mix family monopoly used to flavour beer.
quote: Louis or Lodewijk van Gruuthuse (c. 1427–92) was a statesman and military leader who served under the dukes of Burgundy... His name – and much of his wealth – came from gruut or gruit, a herbal mixture added to beer.

claim: Gruuthusemuseum tells the city's story through more than 600 objects spanning the Burgundian heyday, 17th-18th centuries and 19th-century neo-Gothic rediscovery.
quote: The former 15th-century city palace is a unique museum where visitors can discover the city's rich past through the stories behind more than six hundred objects.

claim: The Beaufort Triennial is a contemporary-art event that has been placing sculpture along the 67-km Flemish coast since 2003; the next edition is expected in 2027.
quote: Beaufort is a triennial contemporary art event that has been transforming the Flemish coast since 2003.

claim: Beaufort 2024 (27 March – 3 November 2024) on the theme 'Fabric of Life' featured 18 artists with two works per coastal municipality and drew about 1.7 million visitors.
quote: The eighth edition of the Beaufort Triennial attracted about 1.7 million visitors.

claim: Over 40 works from past Beaufort editions are permanently installed and free to view 24/7; landmarks include Arne Quinze's 'Rock Strangers' in Ostend and 'Men' that emerges with the tide in Nieuwpoort.
quote: All sculptures are located in public spaces and are free to view and can be visited 24/7.

claim: Knokke-Heist's own 'Sculpture Link' trail places 14 contemporary works along the seafront from Heldenplein in Heist to De Wielingen in Het Zoute.
quote: Sculpture Link places 14 contemporary art works along the seafront, from Heldenplein in Heist to De Wielingen in Het Zoute.

claim: Damme styles itself a book village with a themed book market on the second Sunday of every month and resident bookshops including Boeken Diogenes, Maerlant and Feniks.
quote: A themed book market takes place in Damme every second Sunday of the month.

claim: Charles De Coster's 1867 novel sets the legendary Tijl Uilenspiegel's birth in Damme, anchoring the town's literary identity around a figure of Flemish resistance.
quote: In Damme, in Flanders, when the May month opened the blossoms on the hagedoorns, Uilenspiegel, Klaas's son, was born.

claim: The Damse Vaart canal path between Bruges and Damme is a flat, well-paved 7 km route lined with century-old poplars, ideal for walking or cycling.
quote: The ride is about 7 kilometers one way... There's a perfectly flat, well-paved cycle path running parallel to the water.

claim: The Damse Vaart was dug from 1810 on Napoleon's order as part of a military supply network and is now a beloved cycling, walking and boating route.
quote: In 1810, the Damse Vaart was commissioned by Napoleon as part of a larger network of military supply routes.

claim: The 'Lamme Goedzak' paddle-steamer runs four return trips a day between Bruges and Damme along the canal.
quote: The 'Lamme Goedzak' taking you four times a day from Bruges to Damme and back.

claim: Sincfala, housed in an 1899 neo-Gothic fishermen's school in Heist, tells 2,000 years of Zwinstreek history with a scale model of medieval Sluis and the shrimp boat Jessica in the garden.
quote: Sincfala is the old name for 'het Zwin'... a unique scale model of the harbour town of Sluis in around 1400.

claim: The For Freedom Museum at Ramskapellestraat 91/93, Knokke-Heist, focuses on the liberation of West Flanders and the Battle of the Scheldt through artefacts, mannequins and audio-guided testimonies.
quote: This military museum specializes in World War II history, specifically highlighting the liberation of West Flanders and the Battle of the Scheldt.

claim: Brothers Danny and Freddy Jones run the For Freedom Museum in memory of their father Dennis Jones, a British Normandy veteran who married a Knokke-Heist girl in 1947, focusing on Canadian liberation units.
quote: Brothers Danny and Freddy Jones are the sons of the late Dennis Jones, a British Normandy veteran from Crewe, Cheshire (UK), who married a girl from Knokke-Heist in 1947.

claim: The Knokke-Heist Cartoon Festival 2026 returns to CC Scharpoord 21 March – 3 May 2026 with 250+ cartoons on the theme 'Together Cartoonist', free admission, daily 10–18h.
quote: Starting in 2026, the Cartoon Festival will move from summer to spring and from Ravelingen back to CC Scharpoord.

claim: The 51st Knokke Art Fair (KNAF) is scheduled for August 2026 and bills itself as the first art fair held inside an artwork.
quote: The 51st edition of Knokke Art Fair awaits in 2026.

claim: Musea Brugge's new BRUSK art gallery opens to the public from 8 May 2026, joining the umbrella network of historic museums.
quote: You can visit BRUSK from 8 May 2026, when the art gallery opens its doors to the general public.
